script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Monday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed two point three seven percent up on the session. A strong open to August, with broad-based gains across technology and communication services driving the move.

Alphabet is up nearly five percent and facing a fresh federal lawsuit — a damages claim that could set the terms of the post-antitrust ruling era for the world's dominant digital ad business. The legal exposure is real, and the market shrugged it off anyway.

The Nasdaq Composite rose two point one three percent on Monday's session, with technology and communication services leading the advance. Investors appeared to respond positively to signals out of Washington that the United States would restart diplomatic talks with Iran, easing near-term geopolitical risk and sending oil lower while equities climbed broadly.

Alphabet's session gain of four point eight eight percent came alongside a material legal development. Teads Holding Company filed suit in the Southern District of New York seeking financial damages from Google LLC and Alphabet, following a federal court ruling in the Eastern District of Virginia that found Google had engaged in unlawful anticompetitive practices in the digital advertising market. The complaint is seeking damages and other legal remedies — figures not yet disclosed. Analyst Ray Wang, commenting separately on the hyperscaler landscape, argued that Alphabet and its peers remain the clearest structural winners in artificial intelligence deployment. For this portfolio, Alphabet sits at six point one eight percent of total weight. Monday's price action suggests the market is treating the legal overhang as manageable, but the damages phase of this litigation is just beginning.

Now the full holdings rundown, starting at the top. Nvidia was up two point nine three percent on Monday's session. The broader chip sector rallied to open August, with the Nasdaq's two point one three percent gain pulling chipmakers higher alongside it. Cboe senior vice president JJ Kinahan, appearing Monday evening, noted that demand conditions for key chipmakers remain in focus as earnings season moves into semiconductor territory this week. Watch Advanced Micro Devices' results closely — they report earnings this week and the read-through for Nvidia will matter.

Apple was down one point seven eight percent on Monday's session. That makes it the weakest performer in this portfolio by a significant margin. A Reuters report circulating during the session indicated Apple is testing memory chips from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, a company that recently completed an initial public offering and has surged to a market valuation approaching five hundred billion dollars. That is a direct competitive threat to the memory suppliers Apple currently sources from, and the market flagged concern. One analyst piece out Monday raised the longer-term argument that Microsoft may surpass Apple in total market valuation within eighteen months. Apple carries six point eight zero percent of this portfolio.

Alphabet was covered in the top story. Four point eight eight percent to the upside. Monitor the damages proceedings closely.

Micron was up zero point seven nine percent on Monday's session. The stock recovered from early losses as the broader chip sector gained, but the ChangXin Memory Technologies competitive threat loomed over the name all session. Reuters reported that ChangXin is evaluating a second memory chip facility in Beijing. Micron investors are being asked to hold a long-term view while near-term competitive noise intensifies.

Microsoft was up four point nine three percent on Monday's session — the strongest single-session gain among primary holdings. No company-specific catalyst was identified, but analyst commentary positioned Microsoft and fellow hyperscalers as the clearest artificial intelligence infrastructure beneficiaries. That framing appears to have resonated with institutional buyers on Monday.

Amazon was up four point five eight percent on Monday's session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average hit a record, and Amazon was cited as a driver of that milestone. No earnings release Monday, but the stock continues to benefit from the same hyperscaler narrative supporting Microsoft.

Advanced Micro Devices was up one point seven eight percent on Monday's session. The company is scheduled to report quarterly earnings this week — one of the most anticipated prints in the semiconductor space given the current demand environment. That event is the single most important near-term catalyst for this name.

Tesla was up three point four nine percent on Monday's session. No company-specific news drove the move. The broader risk-on tone and geopolitical de-escalation signal from Washington appeared to lift consumer discretionary broadly. Tesla has no major catalyst immediately visible, but the macro backdrop shifted favorably on Monday.

Intel was up zero point eight nine percent on Monday's session. The stock participated in the broader chip rally but underperformed the sector average. No specific news catalyst. Watch for any read-through from Advanced Micro Devices' earnings this week that touches on the competitive server and data center processor landscape.

Three things to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Advanced Micro Devices reports quarterly earnings this week — the print and forward guidance will set the tone for the entire semiconductor complex. Second, SpaceX reports its first-ever quarterly earnings on Tuesday — a historic event for the space and industrials sector with potential ripple effects across growth names. Third, monitor developments in the Teads versus Alphabet litigation for any early indication of damages scope, which could move Alphabet materially.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Advanced Micro Devices' earnings report will be the number one event to watch when markets open Tuesday.
